chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAllān, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Which is more excellent in the last two rakʿahs, recitation or tasbīḥ? He said: Recitation is more excellent.
So the correct way to understand this narration is that when he is an Imam, recitation is more excellent; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more excellent or superior in merit
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحُ: glorification formula recited in place of Qur'anic recitation
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the last two units of a four-rakʿah prayer
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: recitation in salat, as opposed to tasbīḥ in the final two rakʿahs

ai.seo_question: In the last two rakʿahs of salat, is recitation better than tasbīḥ?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling regarding what is preferable in the final two rakʿahs of salat: recitation or tasbīḥ. It states that recitation is more excellent, and the appended clarification explains this as applying to the case where the person is leading as Imam.
